Next, look at strengthening the tests so they would catch mutations of the fix, for example by covering the other cases the issue lists…

survivors.description: Evaluates the forward ref with empty globals, so module-level names fail to resolve.
survivors.diff:
--- a/mashumaro/jsonschema/schema.py
+++ b/mashumaro/jsonschema/schema.py
@@ -667,3 +667,3 @@
     try:
-        return evaluate_forward_ref(forward_ref, globalns, {})
+        return evaluate_forward_ref(forward_ref, {}, {})
     except Exception:
survivors.words: mashumaro/jsonschema/schema.py:668: changing `        return evaluate_forward_ref(forward_ref, globalns, {...` to `        return evaluate_forward_ref(forward_ref, {}, {})` made no test fail; not compared with the fix: no compared function in its file

survivors.description: Returns None instead of the original forward ref when evaluation fails.
survivors.diff:
--- a/mashumaro/jsonschema/schema.py
+++ b/mashumaro/jsonschema/schema.py
@@ -671,3 +671,3 @@
         # This preserves backward compatibility
-        return forward_ref
+        return None
survivors.words: mashumaro/jsonschema/schema.py:672: changing `        return forward_ref` to `        return None` made no test fail; not compared with the fix: no compared function in its file

survivors.description: Passes instance.type instead of origin_type as the owner, which can give the wrong module for generic aliases.
survivors.diff:
--- a/mashumaro/jsonschema/schema.py
+++ b/mashumaro/jsonschema/schema.py
@@ -686,3 +686,3 @@
         if isinstance(resolved_v, ForwardRef):
-            resolved_v = _evaluate_forward_ref(resolved_v, instance.origin_type)
+            resolved_v = _evaluate_forward_ref(resolved_v, instance.type)
         annotations[k] = resolved_v
